title: Living ashtpadi 24
hook: the psalm ends where it began: peace in remembering

segments.voice: Yesterday, the ambrosial Name, and your line: the name is peace. Did you set down one load on a single breath? Today we live the last ashtpadi, and find that Sukhmani has been walking in a circle all along. Day five hundred thirty-three.
screen: `THE AMBROSIAL NAME — THE NAME IS PEACE.`

segments.voice: A round is a song that chases itself. One voice starts, a second joins a line later, then a third, and the tune keeps circling back to its own beginning. Children learn them at camp around a fire. The fun is that there's no real ending: when you reach the last line, you're already back at the first. Sukhmani is long, twenty-four ashtpadis, more than an hour to recite at an unhurried pace. But when you reach the last one, you find you've come back around. It ends where it began.
screen: `A SONG THAT CHASES ITSELF.` → `NO REAL ENDING.` → `BACK WHERE IT BEGAN.`

segments.voice: Here's the twenty-fourth ashtpadi in brief. Its salok rings pooraa four times: the perfect Lord, perfect Name, perfect One found and praised. Its first stanza calls us to the perfect Guru's teaching and to remember God with every breath, so the mind's anxiety lifts. And over it all hangs Sukhmani's center line: the jewel of peace is the ambrosial Name. Now go back to the very first stanza of Sukhmani, all the way at the start. It opens with a famous run of one word: simrau simar simar sukh paavau. In paraphrase: I remember, remembering, remembering, I find peace, and the troubles of the body are erased. Simran: remembering, keeping God in mind. And sukh: peace. That's the first line. Twenty-four ashtpadis later, the bani closes on the same two things: the Name, remembered, and the peace it brings. It ends where it began. Why does that matter for daily life? Because a circle tells you something a straight line doesn't. A straight line says: finish this, and you're done. A circle says: this is a path you walk again. Sikhs who recite Sukhmani don't read it once and file it away. Many recite it daily, or weekly, or gather to recite it together. Each time, the first line and the last line meet. Living ashtpadi 24 isn't reaching a finish. It's coming back around to remembering, and finding the peace was waiting there the whole time.
screen: `THE LAST ASHTPADI: PERFECT, BREATH BY BREATH.` · `SIMRAU SIMAR SIMAR: THE FIRST LINE.` · `THE SAME TWO THINGS AT THE END.` · `A CIRCLE YOU WALK AGAIN.` · then, large: `PEACE IN REMEMBERING.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: remember, and rest. Sit and let the breath settle. For the first minute, remember, gently: someone who loves you, a time you felt held, a moment of beauty. If you pray, remember God, and let Waheguru come with the breath, like the first line of Sukhmani: remembering, remembering. For the second minute, stop remembering and just rest in whatever peace the remembering left behind. The bell holds the time.
Living ashtpadi 24. Sukhmani opens with simran bringing sukh, remembering bringing peace, and closes on the same Name and the same peace.
Your line: peace in remembering. Today, at the start and at the end of your day, take three breaths of remembering, so the day comes full circle. Day five hundred thirty-three.

howItsDone: Sukhmani Sahib opens with simran bringing peace and closes on the same Name, and many Sikhs recite it daily or weekly, alone or together, returning to that circle.

fork.setup: you finish the twenty-fourth ashtpadi. by today's lesson, what have you reached?
options: the end; you're done for good.
the beginning again: remembering, and peace.
fork.reveal: Sukhmani is a circle: it opens with simran bringing sukh, and closes on the same Name and peace.

original.note: Gurmukhi: simran, remembering God; Sukhmani's first line repeats simar, remember.

trapdoor: what you thought: living ashtpadi 24 means finishing Sukhmani.
what it means: coming back to where it began, remembering the Name and finding peace, again and again.
what a scholar hears: Sukhmani's opening line, simrau simar simar sukh paavau, triples the root simar, and its closing ashtpadi returns to the Name and peace.
